papers.title: Design and computational investigation of a polyaniline-pyrrole copolymer and its antimicrobial and cytotoxic properties.
papers.abstract: The present study focused on the single-pot synthesis of polyaniline (PANI) and polyaniline-pyrrole (PANI-Py) copolymer via the chemical oxidative polymerization method (COPM). The structural features of synthesised PANI and PANI-Py were characterised using UV-visible and FTIR spectroscopy. The thermal stability of synthesised PANI and PANI-Py copolymer was examined by TGA and DSC over the temperature range of 33-1000 °C. BET and viscosity measurements analysed surface area and molecular weight. Conductivity of PANI and PANI-Py was measured by a two-probe method. DFT calculations confirmed the
papers.summary: This study synthesizes a polyaniline-pyrrole copolymer via chemical oxidative polymerization and characterizes its structural, thermal, and conductive properties using spectroscopy, thermal analysis, and DFT calculations. The authors also evaluate its antimicrobial and cytotoxic activity, suggesting potential biomedical applications for the conducting copolymer.

papers.title: Spontaneous Phase Separation in Polymer Solution by Janus Nanoparticle Compatibilizers: An Atomistic Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: We perform atomistic molecular dynamics simulations in order to investigate the structural and dynamic properties of Janus gold nanoparticles within diverse solvent environments, specifically pure polyethylene, pure water, and mixed polyethylene/water matrices. The nanoparticles, approximately 7 nm in diameter and almost totally surrounded by (211) surfaces at the thermodynamic limit, are functionalized with hydrophobic polyethylene chains on one hemisphere and hydrophilic poly-(ethylene oxide) chains on the other. In mixed systems, the Janus nanoparticle acts as an effective stabilizer, direc
papers.summary: This study uses atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to examine how Janus gold nanoparticles (with hydrophobic polyethylene on one hemisphere and hydrophilic poly(ethylene oxide) on the other) behave in pure polyethylene, pure water, and mixed polyethylene/water environments. The authors find that in mixed systems the Janus nanoparticles act as effective compatibilizers, directing the spontaneous phase separation of the polymer solution.

papers.title: Unraveling the Complex Hydrogen-Bonding and Solvation Patterns of Fructose Tautomers via Complementary AIMD and Classical MD Simulations.
papers.abstract: Understanding the molecular-level hydration of fructose tautomers remains a challenge due to their rapid interconversion and structural complexity. A dual-scale approach was employed, combining long-time classical molecular dynamics (MD) and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) to elucidate differences in the hydrogen-bonding networks of both pyranose and furanose tautomers with statistical and electronic accuracy. Our simulations highlight the inherent competition between intra- and intermolecular hydrogen bonds, driven by the limited number of hydroxyl donor and acceptor sites. Crucially, the
papers.summary: This study combines classical molecular dynamics and ab initio molecular dynamics to characterize how fructose's pyranose and furanose tautomers interact with water through hydrogen bonding. The simulations reveal a competition between intramolecular and intermolecular hydrogen bonds, driven by the limited number of hydroxyl donor and acceptor sites on each tautomer.

papers.title: Solvent Extraction for Heavy Oil from Carbonate AsphaltsExperiment and Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: We have systematically studied the effects of solvents such as benzene, toluene, isooctane, and cyclooctane on the selective separation of four heavy oil components (saturates, aromatics, resins, asphaltenes), aiming to clarify the molecular mechanism of solvent extraction as an oil-solid separation method in heavy oil extraction. However, the time-dependent extraction kinetics and the detachment behavior of different saturates, aromatics, resins, and asphaltenes (SARA) fractions from mineral surfaces under solvent action remain insufficiently understood. In this work, solvent extraction exper
papers.summary: This study investigates how different solvents (benzene, toluene, isooctane, cyclooctane) selectively extract heavy oil components (saturates, aromatics, resins, asphaltenes) from carbonate asphalt surfaces. Combining experiments with molecular dynamics simulations, the authors clarify the molecular mechanisms and kinetics of solvent-based oil-solid separation. The work provides insight into optimizing solvent extraction for heavy oil recovery from carbonate reservoirs.

papers.title: Predicting Oncogenic Mutants of Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor in Lung Cancer by Molecular Dynamics Simulation with Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is a frequently mutated protein kinase found in patients suffering from non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although therapeutic drugs targeting EGFR are available, not all patients respond to these drugs, and it is not yet known whether some clinically detected mutations are actionable. Although the oncogenicity of some mutants is well established, many mutants found in patients are not yet classified or classified as Variants of Uncertain Significance. For newly discovered rare mutants, strong evidence supporting their classification into oncogenic
papers.summary: This study combines molecular dynamics simulations with machine learning to predict whether EGFR mutations found in lung cancer patients are oncogenic. The approach aims to help classify variants of uncertain significance, which could guide treatment decisions for non-small cell lung cancer.

papers.title: Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Monoterpene Phenol Dimers from Satureja bachtiarica.
papers.abstract: Satureja bachtiarica (Bakhtiari savory) is an aromatic herb cultivated both as a culinary spice and for its medicinal uses. Species of Satureja are known to exhibit anti-inflammatory properties. Monoterpene phenol dimers with biphenyl skeletons have been identified in these plants and structural investigations revealed the key role of the biphenyl scaffold in interacting with MAPEG family proteins. Thus, in the present contribution, we investigated by biochemical and cell-based assays, together with molecular docking and molecular dynamics investigations, the modulation of inflammatory mediato
papers.summary: This study investigates monoterpene phenol dimers from the aromatic herb Satureja bachtiarica, focusing on their anti-inflammatory properties. Using biochemical and cell-based assays alongside molecular docking and dynamics simulations, the authors show that the biphenyl scaffold of these compounds interacts with MAPEG family proteins to modulate inflammatory mediators. The findings support the traditional medicinal use of Satureja species and highlight these dimers as potential anti-inflammatory leads.

papers.title: Insights into the Solution Structure and Oligomeric State of Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate Aldolase and Pyruvate Kinase from Nakaseomyces glabratus by Small-Angle X‑ray Scattering (SAXS) and AlphaFold Prediction.
papers.abstract: Nakaseomyces glabratus is an opportunistic pathogen of humans, causing invasive candidiasis (IC). Among the risk factors that favor IC are various host-specific factors. Although drugs are available to treat candidiasis, their clinical application remains limited. Therefore, it is necessary to identify therapeutic targets that will enable the development of new antifungals. In this regard, our research group has identified enzymes as potential therapeutic targets in N. glabratus, including fructose-1,6-bisphosphate aldolase (Fba1) and pyruvate kinase (Pk). Enzyme activity studies on these two
papers.summary: This study uses small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) combined with AlphaFold structure prediction to characterize the solution structure and oligomeric state of two glycolytic enzymes, fructose-1,6-bisphosphate aldolase (Fba1) and pyruvate kinase (Pk), from the opportunistic fungal pathogen Nakaseomyces glabratus. The work aims to validate these enzymes as potential targets for new antifungal drugs against invasive candidiasis.

papers.title: Alchemical Free Energy Perturbation Predicts Relative Binding Affinities of Propofol Analogs and Etomidate Stereoisomers at the GABAAR.
papers.abstract: General anesthetics such as propofol and etomidate exert their clinical effects primarily through positive allosteric modulation of γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptors (GABAAR). Despite decades of research, the quantitative structure-activity relationships governing anesthetic binding remain incompletely characterized at the atomic level. Here, we employ rigorous alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations using a CHARMm GPU-accelerated protocol to compute relative binding free energies for a series of 13 propofol analogs at the wild-type GABAAR, as well as for the stereoisomeric p
papers.summary: This study uses alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations to predict relative binding affinities of 13 propofol analogs and etomidate stereoisomers at the GABA-A receptor. The work demonstrates that rigorous physics-based FEP can quantitatively capture structure-activity relationships for general anesthetics at this clinically important target. It provides an atomic-level framework for understanding anesthetic binding that could inform future drug design.

papers.title: Multiscale Investigation of Triboelectric Nanogenerator: An Expanded DFT Calculation Based on Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Various types of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have been proposed, which rely on the details of electron transfer, ion migration, and mechanochemistry, but their largely different scales complicate the quantitative analysis of their contributions. In this study, we first investigate the electron transfer behavior at the nanoscale using density functional theory (DFT) calculations for the contact of two typical insulating materials, poly-(vinyl chloride) (PVC) and poly-(vinyl alcohol) (PVA), with an adsorbed water layer in between. The DFT results are then used to construct machine learn
papers.summary: This study combines density functional theory (DFT) calculations with machine learning to model electron transfer at the nanoscale interface between two insulating polymers (PVC and PVA) with an adsorbed water layer, aiming to understand triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) behavior across scales. The DFT results are used to train machine learning models that extend the analysis to larger scales, addressing the challenge of bridging nanoscale electron transfer with macroscopic TENG performance.

papers.title: Exploring the Inhibitory Effects of Some Detergents on Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis with Specific Focus on Zwitterionic Sulfobetaines.
papers.abstract: Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis (MAP) infects ruminants with Johne's disease and is also involved in human inflammatory bowel syndrome, such as Crohn's disease. With increasing drug resistance and zoonosis, there is a critical need for novel antimicrobial compounds having the potential to inhibit disease-causing bacteria. The present work examines the antimycobacterial activity of six detergent-like compounds, among which four are sulfobetaine-based zwitterionic detergents: amidosulfobetaine-14 (ASB-14), lauryl sulfobetaine (DDAPS), caprylyl sulfobetaine (D4266), and sulfobetai
papers.summary: This study tests six detergent-like compounds, including four zwitterionic sulfobetaines, for their ability to inhibit the growth of Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis (MAP), a bacterium causing Johne's disease in ruminants and linked to Crohn's disease in humans. The authors identify sulfobetaine-based detergents as having antimycobacterial activity, suggesting a potential new avenue for antimicrobial development against this pathogen.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanism of Ethanol-Acetonitrile Azeotrope Disruption by the Ionic Liquid [BMIM][NTf2].
papers.abstract: Ionic liquids (ILs) have attracted significant attention as green solvents for azeotrope separation via extractive distillation; however, the microscopic mechanism by which ILs eliminate azeotropic phenomena remains inadequately understood. This study employs a combination of spectroscopic methods and theoretical calculations to elucidate the mechanism by which 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide ([BMIM][NTf2]) breaks the ethanol-acetonitrile azeotrope. Analysis of the hydroxyl stretching vibration region of ethanol indicates that the ethanol-acetonitrile cross-int
papers.summary: This study uses spectroscopy and theoretical calculations to reveal how the ionic liquid [BMIM][NTf2] breaks the ethanol-acetonitrile azeotrope. The findings show that the ionic liquid disrupts ethanol-acetonitrile cross-interactions by preferentially interacting with ethanol's hydroxyl group, providing a molecular-level explanation for azeotrope elimination in extractive distillation.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis and Antihyperglycemic/Antilipidemic Activities of Quinoline-thiazolidine-2,4-dione Hybrid.
papers.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and hyperlipidemia are interrelated metabolic disorders that significantly increase cardiovascular risk. Thiazolidinediones are known insulin sensitizers, whereas quinoline derivatives possess diverse pharmacological activities. To explore their complementary activity, we designed a novel hybrid compound integrating a thiazolidinedione core with a quinoline moiety via a carbon spacer. Materials and Methods: The hybrid molecule was synthesized through a straightforward route and structurally confirmed by spectroscopic analyses. Zebrafish (Danio rerio)
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of a hybrid molecule combining a thiazolidinedione core (a known insulin-sensitizing scaffold) with a quinoline moiety, connected via a carbon spacer. The compound was structurally characterized and evaluated for antihyperglycemic and antilipidemic activity, with initial testing performed in a zebrafish model. The hybrid represents an early-stage medicinal chemistry effort to develop dual-acting agents for type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia.

papers.title: Benzamides of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles as Anticancer Scaffolds: Synthesis, In Silico and In Vitro Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Indoles and benzimidazoles are important nitrogen-containing heterocyclic scaffolds and are a cornerstone of synthetic drugs. In this study, benzamides of 2-aminophenylindoles and 2-aminophenylbenzimidazoles were synthesized and evaluated for their potential. Further, they were also subjected to computational studies for their ADMET profiling and binding with target proteins. Methods: The synthesized compounds were characterized by ATR-FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR and electrospray ionization mass spectroscopy (ESI-MS). They were screened for their in vitro antibacterial activit
papers.summary: This study synthesized a series of benzamide derivatives of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles and evaluated them for anticancer and antibacterial activity. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically and assessed using in silico ADMET profiling and molecular docking against target proteins, alongside in vitro assays. The work identifies these scaffolds as potential anticancer leads, though the abstract is truncated and full biological data are not fully detailed.

papers.title: Cracking ERα Y537S Resistance: Explainable Machine Learning-Guided Discovery and Molecular Dynamics Validation of Stable Candidate Ligands.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Endocrine resistance due to activating mutations in the estrogen receptor alpha (ERα), especially Y537S, is still a big challenge in the treatment of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, and there is a need to develop new small-molecule inhibitors that can overcome ligand-independent receptor activation. We used an integrated machine learning and molecular dynamics (MD)-based virtual screening (VS) approach to identify potential computationally prioritized hits of ERα Y537S in this study. Methods: The dataset (~3353 compounds) was characterized using molecular finger
papers.summary: This study combines explainable machine learning with molecular dynamics simulations to identify small-molecule inhibitors that can overcome the Y537S mutation in estrogen receptor alpha, a key driver of endocrine resistance in breast cancer. The authors screened ~3,353 compounds and prioritized candidate ligands that remain stably bound to the mutant receptor, offering a computational pipeline for drug discovery against resistant ERα variants.

papers.title: Identification of Small-Molecule Inhibitors of Babesia bovis by High-Throughput SYBR Green I Screening.
papers.abstract: Background: Bovine babesiosis, caused by Babesia bovis, remains a major constraint to cattle production in endemic regions, while the current control relies on only a few drugs with concerns over resistance and residues. Methods: This study screened 9600 chemically diverse compounds from the Drug Discovery Initiative, University of Tokyo, against B. bovis using a 96-well SYBR Green I high-throughput assay at 1 µM. Primary hits were subjected to dose-response testing to determine IC50 values, followed by Madin-Darby bovine kidney cell cytotoxicity assays for selectivity index calculation. Combi
papers.summary: This study screened 9,600 chemically diverse compounds against the cattle parasite Babesia bovis using a high-throughput SYBR Green I assay, identifying primary hits that were then validated with dose-response and cytotoxicity testing to determine IC50 values and selectivity indices. The work provides new candidate small-molecule inhibitors that could expand the limited drug arsenal for bovine babesiosis, a disease constrained by resistance and drug residue concerns.

papers.title: Anti-HIV Potential of Origanum vulgare Compounds Targeting Viral Reverse Transcriptase with High Binding and Stability Validated by Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is one of the viruses that has co-evolved within human populations for a considerable time. With the evolution of new drug-resistant HIV strains, the necessity to discover novel drugs has become an issue of great concern, especially those that have increased binding affinities and inhibitory activity towards RT enzymes. This study used an in silico approach to identify potential HIV-RT inhibitory candidates from Origanum vulgare (oregano). An initial in silico screening of approximately 820 compounds was conducted, and based on molecular docking-derived bindi
papers.summary: This study used computational (in silico) screening of ~820 compounds from oregano (Origanum vulgare) to identify potential inhibitors of HIV reverse transcriptase. Molecular docking and machine learning were used to prioritize compounds with strong binding affinity and stability against the viral enzyme, suggesting oregano-derived molecules as candidate anti-HIV agents warranting further experimental validation.

papers.title: Pangenome-Guided In Silico Design and Structural Evaluation of a Multi-Epitope Vaccine Candidate Against Streptococcus suis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives:Streptococcus suis is an important zoonotic pathogen responsible for severe infections in animals and humans, and the emergence of diverse strains has reduced the effectiveness of conventional antimicrobial therapies. Since there is no broadly protective vaccine, there is a need for new vaccination strategies that focus on conserved antigens from a variety of strains. This study aimed to design and evaluate a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against diverse S. suis strains using an integrated pangenome-guided reverse vaccinology approach. Methods: To design a multi-epitope
papers.summary: This study used a pangenome-guided reverse vaccinology approach to design a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against diverse Streptococcus suis strains, targeting conserved antigens rather than strain-specific ones. The candidate was evaluated in silico, including structural assessment, to predict its potential immunogenicity and stability. The work offers a computational blueprint for a broadly protective vaccine, though experimental validation remains to be done.

papers.title: Confidence-Gated Triage: Coupling Drug-Target Affinity and ADME-T Predictions to Prioritise Compounds for Docking.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Molecular docking and molecular dynamics are accurate but computationally expensive, so the compounds entering them must be chosen well. The present study proposes CADT, a confidence-gated affinity-ADME-T docking-triage cascade that decides which compounds are worth docking. Methods: The gate combines an ensemble estimate of drug-target affinity with its epistemic uncertainty and an applicability-domain check. Predicted absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADME-T) developability is added as a soft flag. All components were trained on openly lice
papers.summary: The paper introduces CADT, a triage cascade that uses an ensemble drug-target affinity model with uncertainty estimates and an applicability-domain check, plus a soft ADME-T developability flag, to decide which compounds are worth running through expensive docking and molecular dynamics. The goal is to prioritize compounds more efficiently by gating on prediction confidence rather than raw affinity alone.

papers.title: Integrated Machine Learning and Molecular Simulation-Guided Discovery of Novel Small-Molecule PD-L1 Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The programmed death-1/programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-1/PD-L1) immune checkpoint is a key therapeutic target in cancer immunotherapy, but small-molecule inhibition remains challenging due to its shallow and dynamic interaction interface. This study aimed to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-guided workflow to identify novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting the PD-L1 dimer interface. Methods: A combined computational and experimental approach was established. A support vector regression-genetic algorithm (SVR-GA) model was trained on a dataset of 1385 known PD-L1
papers.summary: This study developed an AI-guided workflow combining support vector regression-genetic algorithm modeling with molecular simulation to discover novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting the PD-L1 dimer interface for cancer immunotherapy. The approach was validated experimentally, demonstrating the utility of integrating machine learning with physics-based simulation for hit discovery against challenging shallow protein-protein interaction interfaces.

papers.title: Biopharmaceutical Profiling of Herpetrione: A BCS II Properties and P-gp Substrate Guiding Nanoparticle Design.
papers.abstract: Objectives: Herpetrione (HPE) is a bioactive lignan recognized for its hepatoprotective properties; however, it exhibits limited oral bioavailability. This study aimed to classify HPE within the framework of the biopharmaceutics classification system (BCS) and to develop a nanoparticle formulation. Methods: To this end, a comprehensive investigation was conducted, encompassing computer prediction analysis, equilibrium solubility measurements across the gastrointestinal pH range, Caco-2 bidirectional transportation, in situ single-pass intestinal perfusion (SPIP), and molecular docking with P-g
papers.summary: This study characterizes herpetrione (HPE), a hepatoprotective lignan, as a BCS Class II compound with poor solubility and identifies it as a P-glycoprotein substrate. Based on these properties, the authors designed a nanoparticle formulation to improve its oral bioavailability.

papers.title: Enantiomer-Resolved Biological Profiling and Chiral Developability Assessment of Novel Naphthylethyl Thioureas.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Stereochemistry can substantially influence the biological activity and pharmaceutical properties of small molecules. This study investigated the stereochemistry-dependent biological activity and chiral recognition of novel naphthylethyl thiourea enantiomers using an integrated biological, chromatographic, and computational approach. Methods: Ten pairs of naphthylethyl thiourea enantiomers were synthesized from enantiomerically pure precursors and characterized. Antiproliferative and antibacterial activity, chiral HPLC behavior on polysaccharide- and protein-based statio
papers.summary: This study synthesized and characterized ten pairs of naphthylethyl thiourea enantiomers, then profiled their antiproliferative and antibacterial activities alongside chiral HPLC behavior and computational analysis. The work demonstrates that stereochemistry significantly influences biological activity and chiral recognition, highlighting the importance of enantiomer-resolved profiling in drug development.

papers.title: Phloretin Modulates STING Ubiquitination Degradation to Restrain Dendritic Cell Overactivation and Alleviate Sjögren's Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sjögren's Syndrome (SS) is an autoimmune disorder with impaired exocrine gland function. Its pathogenesis remains elusive, but aberrant innate/adaptive immunity and dysregulated interferon signaling are core features. Current SS research lacks exploration of innate immune mechanisms and therapeutic targets. Phloretin, a natural dihydrochalcone derivative, inhibits excessive innate immune activation, yet its role and mechanism in SS remain unreported. Methods: This study aimed to explore the therapeutic efficacy of phloretin against Sjögren's syndrome (SS) and elucidate t
papers.summary: This study shows that phloretin, a natural plant compound, reduces overactivation of dendritic cells by promoting the ubiquitination and degradation of STING, a key innate immune signaling protein. In a Sjögren's syndrome model, this effect alleviated disease features, suggesting STING regulation as a potential therapeutic target for this autoimmune disorder.

papers.title: Extraction, Phytochemical Profiling, and Computational Evaluation of Corymbia citriodora Essential Oil as a COX-2 Inhibitor: Steam vs. Microwave-Assisted Distillation, GC-MS/MS, Docking, DFT, and MD Simulations.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Chronic inflammation sustained by cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) underlies many human diseases, while the cardiovascular liabilities of coxibs have renewed interest in plant-derived alternatives. This study characterised the volatile composition of Corymbia citriodora essential oil under two distillation regimes and identified constituents able to inhibit human COX-2 and iNOS. Methods: Oils obtained by steam distillation (SD) and microwave-assisted steam distillation (MSD) were profiled by GC-MS/MS. All identified constituents were sc
papers.summary: This study compared steam distillation and microwave-assisted steam distillation for extracting Corymbia citriodora essential oil, profiling the volatile compounds by GC-MS/MS. Computational docking, DFT, and molecular dynamics simulations identified oil constituents capable of inhibiting COX-2 and iNOS, suggesting plant-derived alternatives to coxibs for inflammation.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology and Molecular Simulation Reveal Potential Targets and Pathways of Vine Tea in Feline Intestinal Inflammation.
papers.abstract: Feline intestinal inflammation is a common gastrointestinal disorder in cats and is associated with immune dysregulation, epithelial barrier injury, microbial imbalance, and persistent inflammatory signaling. This entirely in silico study investigated predicted molecular associations between vine tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata) constituents and feline intestinal inflammation using network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation. No feline cells, tissues, animals, or clinical samples were used. Candidate compounds were screened and evaluated with SwissADME as a computa
papers.summary: This purely computational study used network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict how compounds in vine tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata) might interact with molecular targets involved in feline intestinal inflammation. No feline cells, tissues, or animals were used, so all findings are predictions requiring experimental validation. The work nominates candidate targets and pathways that could guide future in vitro or in vivo studies.

papers.title: Accelerating Cosmetic Innovation Through Next-Generation Computational Toxicology: From Structural Alerts to Molecular Dynamics and Artificial Intelligence for Skin Sensitization Assessment.
papers.abstract: Skin sensitization remains a critical toxicological endpoint in cosmetic ingredient development, particularly under accelerated innovation cycles and increasingly stringent safety requirements. Although NAMs have achieved substantial regulatory maturity for this endpoint, most computational approaches-including structural alerts, read-across, and quantitative structure-activity relationship models-rely predominantly on chemical structure and statistical associations, with limited representation of the molecular processes underlying sensitization. This perspective proposes a transparent and tes
papers.summary: This perspective argues that current computational toxicology methods for assessing skin sensitization—such as structural alerts and QSAR models—rely too heavily on chemical structure and statistical correlations rather than the underlying molecular mechanisms. The authors propose integrating molecular dynamics simulations and artificial intelligence to build more transparent, mechanistically grounded next-generation models for cosmetic ingredient safety assessment.

papers.title: Resnet-Driven In Silico Identification of Lead Peptides from the Venom Gland Transcriptome of Orientothele washanensis Coupled with Molecular Docking and Dynamics Simulation.
papers.abstract: Background: Orientothele washanensis is a venomous spider with considerable ecological and scientific importance. Its venom, characterized by complex composition and ease of collection, serves as a valuable resource for the discovery of natural peptide drugs. Conventional wet-lab screening methods are limited by rigorous experimental conditions, high resource consumption, and long research cycles, which hinder the efficient identification of functional peptides from the venom gland transcriptome of this spider. Methods: To address these technical bottlenecks, this study developed a novel deep
papers.summary: This study uses a ResNet deep learning model to screen the venom gland transcriptome of the spider Orientothele washanensis for potential peptide drug leads, then validates top candidates with molecular docking and dynamics simulations. The work demonstrates an in silico pipeline that could bypass costly and slow wet-lab screening for natural peptide discovery.

papers.title: Systems Biology and Structure-Based In Silico Evaluations of Quercetin-Psychobiotic Interactions for the Management of Depression.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Psychobiotics are live microorganisms that, when administered in appropriate amounts, can enhance mental health. Through the production of neuroactive metabolites, regulation of immune responses, and interactions along the gut-brain axis, they modulate host neurophysiology. However, significant strain-specific variability exists in their metabolic capabilities, colonization potential, and functional interactions, necessitating a systematic approach for psychobiotic strain selection. Methods: In the present study, an integrated in silico systems biology approach combining
papers.summary: This study uses integrated in silico systems biology and structure-based methods to evaluate how quercetin, a plant flavonoid, interacts with psychobiotic bacteria for managing depression. It aims to systematically assess strain-specific metabolic and functional interactions along the gut-brain axis to guide psychobiotic strain selection. The work is computational and preliminary, proposing a framework rather than providing experimental validation.

papers.title: Synthesis, Spectroscopic Characterization, Molecular Docking Studies Toward the GABAA Receptor, ADMET Prediction, GABA Aminotransferase Inhibition, and Anxiolytic Evaluation of Novel Thiazine Derivatives.
papers.abstract: Background: The current study uses a computational technique to investigate synthesized thiazine compounds that exhibit potential interactions with the GABAA receptor. A series of novel thiazine derivatives was synthesized via the cyclization reaction of chalcone with thiourea. Methods: For the synthesized compounds, spectroscopic characterization, namely FT-IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and mass spectrometry, was carried out. In addition, the AutoDock Vina 4.2 software was applied to carry out an in silico docking study. Results: The synthesized compounds C3 and C6 exhibited comparable predicted docki
papers.summary: This study synthesized a series of novel thiazine derivatives and characterized them using standard spectroscopic techniques. Computational docking against the GABAA receptor, ADMET predictions, and GABA aminotransferase inhibition assays identified compounds C3 and C6 as promising anxiolytic candidates with favorable binding and drug-like properties.

papers.title: Identification and Preliminary mRNA Validation of Key Genes Associated with Tolerogenic Dendritic Cells in Keloid Based on Transcriptome Data.
papers.abstract: Keloid is a cutaneous fibrotic disorder characterized by excessive fibrous tissue proliferation during wound healing. Tolerogenic dendritic cells (tolDCs) may participate in keloid immunopathology, but the related molecular signatures remain unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate tolDC-associated genes in keloid by integrating tolDC-related transcriptomic profiles with keloid transcriptomic datasets.
papers.summary: This study integrates tolerogenic dendritic cell (tolDC) transcriptomic profiles with keloid transcriptome datasets to identify candidate genes linking tolDCs to keloid pathology. The authors identify key tolDC-associated genes and perform preliminary mRNA validation, suggesting a role for tolDC-related immune mechanisms in keloid formation. The findings are exploratory and require further experimental validation.

papers.title: MAFF as a potential novel protective factor against Parkinson's disease: evidence from Mendelian randomization and single-cell RNA sequencing.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder. Although MAFF may be involved in PD, the mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the potential mechanisms of MAFF in PD and identify novel therapeutic targets.
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization and single-cell RNA sequencing to investigate whether the transcription factor MAFF protects against Parkinson's disease. The findings suggest MAFF may act as a novel protective factor, offering a potential new therapeutic target for PD.
